newsitem.title: CANADA: Kmart sells Kmart Canada for C$185 mln.
newsitem.headline: Kmart sells Kmart Canada for C$185 mln.

text.p: U.S.-based Kmart Corp said on Monday it sold most of its Kmart Canada Co unit to an investor group comprising York Management Services Inc, Capital d'Amerique CDPQ Inc and Cherokee Ventures Canada Inc for C$185 million.
Troubled Kmart Canada, the nation's third largest discount retailer, has been awaiting a savior for years. Troy, Michigan-based Kmart said it kept a 12.5 percent equity stake.

Also, Kmart Canada secured a new C$135 million line of credit from Congress Financial Corp. The new owners appointed George Heller, former Bata Industries North America and Europe president, as president and chief executive officer.

The investor group includes the Capital d'Amerique CDPQ Inc, which is a wholly owned unit of Caisse de depot et placement du Quebec. The Quebec-based Caisse is a public-sector pension funds manager. Cherokee Ventures Canada is an arm of Denver-based Cherokee Group which makes private equity direct investments. York Management Services is a New Jersey-based investment and management firm.

Kmart Corp President and Chief Executive Floyd Hall said that the sale "is in keeping with our commitment to focus on our core U.S.-based operations and continue improving our overall financial performance."

Kmart Canada posted 1996 sales of more than C$1.1 billion and operates 123 outlets across the nation. It runs third in Canada's C$12 billion discount retail sector behind Wal-Mart Canada Inc, wholly-owned by Wal-Mart Stores Inc, and Hudson's Bay Co's unit Zellers.

Heller said in a statement that: "Our goal is to create a profitable business through improved customer service, the support of our associates, strengthened information and technology systems, and investment in Kmart Canada's presence and vitality."
Former chief executive Mike Lynch has returned to Kmart's U.S. operations.
